class: measured (one run per case; scratch cwd; Haiku 5.5, effort low; this lane's probe rows only)
preconditions: no other background session had a process (claude agents --json --all: 7 background rows, none with a pid)

cases.start: done, with a process; saved transcript present
steps: claude stop (rc 0): the process ended; state stayed done
claude respawn (rc 0) from a non-interactive shell
cases.after_15_and_90_s: done, idle, a new pid, the same sessionId

cases.start: failed, no process; no saved transcript (its transcript file was created at the respawn)
cases.after_20_and_60_s: done, idle, a new pid, the same sessionId
cases.note: the row's original dispatch prompt was sent again and its command ran again; this disagrees with CHANGELOG 2.1.290 (L794). One observation on a row with an unusual history (a --bg resume of a session open elsewhere): an untested boundary, not a confirmed regression

cases.start: done, no process; saved transcript present; no supervisor running
cases.after_5_and_60_s: no supervisor running; the row done with no process; not in the plain claude agents --json list
cases.note: the respawn started the on-demand supervisor inside the oneshot unit's cgroup, and the unit's exit killed it and the session (systemd's default KillMode=control-group)

steps: the same oneshot unit running systemd-run --user --scope --quiet -- claude respawn <id> (unit rc 0)
cases.after_5_and_60_s: the supervisor running; the row done, idle, with a process, listed by both claude agents --json --all and plain claude agents --json
cases.note: the scope is a sibling of the unit's cgroup, so the supervisor and the session outlive the unit; the tool runs each respawn this way

cleanup: all probe rows stopped and removed (claude stop, claude rm; rc 0); afterwards no background row had a process and the supervisor had exited on its own
not_measured: a failed row WITH a saved transcript after a real shutdown, and the supervisor's start from the real boot unit (its environment and credential source), which wait for the first real boot
